    AI Overview
    Jack Nicklaus is the oldest winner of The Masters, famously winning his sixth Green Jacket in 1986 at 46 years, 2 months, and 23 days old. Known as the "Golden Bear," Nicklaus shot a final-round 65 at age 46 to secure his 18th and final major championship. 
    Key Oldest Masters Winners 
    Jack Nicklaus (1986): 46 years, 82 days 
    Tiger Woods (2019): 43 years, 3 months, 15 days 
    Ben Crenshaw (1995): 43 years, 2 months, 29 days 
    Gary Player (1978): 42 years, 5 months, 8 days 
    Sam Snead (1954): 41 years, 10 months, 16 days 
    Nicklaus has held this record since 1986, with his victory considered one of the greatest comebacks in the tournament's history.

    People also ask
    Who is the oldest guy to win the Masters?
    Nicklaus
    Nicklaus is also the oldest winner of the Masters: he was 46 years 82 days old when he won in 1986. Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods co-hold the record for most consecutive victories with two. Woods was the youngest winner of the Masters, 21 years 104 days old when he won in 1997.
